terms.meaning: India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, which sets rules on personal data, including access and erasure rights.
A user's right to ask for their personal data to be deleted.
A user's right to get a copy of their own data.
The part of the app that receives web requests for a feature and passes them to a service.
A response meaning the request was accepted, which often means work may still be ongoing.
Extra information sent with a web request, such as the browser type.

sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Brings in the NestJS tools for requests, responses, headers and IP addresses, the documentation tags, the signed-in user helper, the compliance service and the request shapes.
sections.why: Likely reason: each import supports the routes below.

sections.name: ComplianceController
sections.title: Compliance routes
sections.what: Defines four routes: request an export with an accepted response, list past export requests, download an export by id, and erase the account with browser and network details recorded.
sections.why: Likely reason: these routes cover the user's access, portability and erasure rights, and the erasure route records proof of who asked.
sections.watch_out: The download route returns all of the user's data inline, so a user with a lot of data will get a very large response.

summary: Provides the compliance routes for requesting a data export, listing exports, downloading an export, and deleting the account.
purpose: Receives requests about the user's own data under DPDP rights and passes them to ComplianceService.
why: Likely reason: DPDP gives users the right to access their data and the right to have it erased, so these routes serve those rights.
how: 1. Requesting an export calls the service and returns an accepted response. 2. Listing returns the user's past export requests. 3. Downloading returns the export data for a given export id. 4. Erasure receives the confirmation text and password, along with the caller's browser and address, and passes them to the service.
inputs: The signed-in user id, the export format in the request body, the export id in the address, and the confirmation and password for erasure. The browser and network address are read from request headers.
outputs: The export request record and data, the list of requests, the export data for download, or the result of erasure.
risks: Download returns the data directly in the response rather than as a file. Each download rebuilds the data, so the result can change over time. The controller does not write its own audit entries and relies on the service.
debug: A 400 response points to a failed input check. For a missing export, check the export id and that it belongs to the user. Check the audit log for export and erasure actions.
